title: Welcome to ValidBridge
summary: ValidBridge is a learning platform for building, teaching and selling courses — including live classes. Start here for the key ideas.
text:
ValidBridge is a cloud learning platform for building courses, teaching them — on demand or live — and selling them. It is built and operated by Stratnovo Systems. Everything you create lives inside an organization: a workspace with its own courses, people, branding and settings. You may belong to one organization or several.
Four ideas you will see everywhere
Course — a program of study. Each course is made of chapters.
Chapter — a module or unit inside a course, containing activities.
Activity — a single piece of learning — a rich page, a video, a document, an assignment, or the recording of a live lesson.
Trail — your personal progress record across every course you have started.
Where to go next
If you want to…Start with
Learn — take courses and join live classesFinding & enrolling in courses
Teach — build a courseCreating a course
Teach live — run a class in LiveBridgeLiveBridge live classes
Sell coursesHow payments work
Run the organizationOrganization settings

Help is always one click away
Open this Help Center from Help in the top bar or the dashboard sidebar. Use the search box at the top of any help page to jump straight to an answer.

title: Accounts, roles & permissions
summary: How you sign in, the four default roles (User, Instructor, Maintainer, Admin) and what each one can do.
text:
You sign in with your email and password, or with another method your organization has enabled (Google, an emailed sign-in link, or single sign-on). Once you are signed in, what you can see and do is decided by your role.
The four default roles
RoleBest forCan do
UserLearnersBrowse and enrol in courses, join live lessons, complete activities and assignments, view their Trail and certificates, and chat with the AI Copilot.
InstructorTeachersEverything a User can do, plus create and edit their own courses, run live lessons, grade assignments, and use the AI authoring tools.
MaintainerTeam leadsManage courses, collections and published content, manage users, and moderate communities and boards.
AdminOwnersFull control of the organization: users and roles, branding, AI, payments, developer settings and every feature.

A role is a bundle of per-resource permissions. Admins can create custom roles, so a title like “Instructor” may be set up differently in your organization. In a live classroom, instructors appear as Lecturer and learners as Student.
Finding your role
Open your account menu (your avatar) and choose Account settings.
If you think you are missing access, ask an admin — they can change your role under Users in the dashboard.
No Dashboard link?
The dashboard is gated by a dashboard access permission. If you do not see a Dashboard link, your role does not include it.

Admins: roles & custom permissions

title: Finding your way around
summary: The learning area, the dashboard, the command palette (Ctrl/⌘ + K) and the onboarding checklist.
text:
ValidBridge has two areas: the learning area that everyone uses, and the dashboard where instructors, maintainers and admins build and manage.
The learning area
Left sidebar — your main destinations: courses, your learning (Trail), live lessons, and any links your organization has added. The logo returns to the organization home.
Top bar — search, help, notifications and your profile. On phones the sidebar folds into a menu.
The dashboard
Open it from the Dashboard link (if your role allows it). Its sidebar groups everything by purpose:
GroupWhat lives there
LearningCourses (including each course’s LiveBridge tab) and assignments
ContentLibrary, communities, podcasts, boards, playgrounds
PeopleUsers, user groups, roles, signups, sign-in methods, two-factor policy, audit logs
MonetizationPayments — overview, offers, payment groups, configuration
AdministrationOrganization settings and developer tools
InsightsAnalytics

The command palette
Press Ctrl K (⌘ K on a Mac) to jump to any page, course, assignment or setting by typing its name.
Open the palette with Ctrl/⌘ + K.
Type a few letters — results are grouped by type.
Use the arrow keys and Enter to open a result, or Esc to close.
Onboarding checklist
New organizations see a short setup checklist in the dashboard (create a course, invite people, brand the workspace…). It disappears once you finish or dismiss it.

title: Searching your organization
summary: Find courses, collections and people across your organization.
text:
Search finds courses, collections and people in your organization. It only ever shows your own organization's content.
Click the search box in the top bar, or open search.
Type a few words from the title or description.
Results are grouped by type; open one to go straight to it.
Looking for help instead?
To search these help articles, use the search box at the top of the Help Center.

title: Create a course
summary: Create a course from the dashboard, add chapters and activities, and publish it when it is ready.
text:
Open the dashboard and go to Courses.
Click New Course. Give it a name, and optionally a description, thumbnail and tags.
The course opens on its General tab. Use Content Structure to add chapters and activities.
When it is ready, publish it from Access & Pricing so learners can see it, and optionally set up SEO and certificates.
Nothing is public by accident
A new course is a draft. Only you and its contributors can see it until you publish it.

Working with others
Add co-authors from the Contributors tab. The editor is real-time, so you can work on the same page at once. To bring in material from another platform, use Course Migration under Courses in the dashboard.
Want to teach it live as well? See Schedule a live lesson.

title: Course settings tabs
summary: What each tab of a course controls: general details, structure, access and pricing, contributors, SEO, certificates, LiveBridge and analytics.
text:
TabWhat it controls
GeneralName, description, thumbnail, tags and other basics.
Content StructureChapters and their activities — where you build the course.
Access & PricingWhether the course is published, and who can open it (everyone, or specific user groups).
ContributorsOther people who can edit the course.
SEOTitle, description and social preview for search engines and shared links.
CertificatesWhether completing the course issues a certificate, and its design.
LiveBridgeLive lessons for this course, their recordings and attendance reports.
AnalyticsEngagement and completion data for this course.

Visibility
Public — listed in the catalogue for everyone in the organization.
Restricted to user groups — visible only to members of chosen groups — for cohorts, internal training or paid bundles.
Draft — not listed; only authors can open it.
To charge for a course, create an offer for it — see Create an offer.
Missing a tab?
Tabs only appear if your role has the matching permission. Ask the course owner or an admin.

title: Chapters & activities
summary: Structure a course into chapters, add activities of different types, and reorder them by dragging.
text:
Courses are organized as course → chapters → activities.
Open the course's Content Structure tab.
Click Add chapter, name it and add an optional description.
Inside a chapter, click Add activity and choose its type.
Drag chapters and activities by their handles to reorder them.
Click an activity to open it and add content.
Choosing an activity type
Dynamic page — written, interactive content built in the block editor.
Video — upload a file or embed from YouTube.
Document — a PDF in the built-in viewer.
Assignment — gradable work. See Create and grade assignments.
SCORM — an uploaded SCORM package, where enabled for your organization.
Live lesson recordings land here too
Recordings of LiveBridge lessons are added to the course as video activities automatically.

title: The content editor
summary: Build pages from blocks: type “/” to insert text, media, quizzes, code playgrounds, callouts and more.
text:
Dynamic pages are written in a block editor: each piece of content is a block you can move, duplicate or delete.
Insert a block
Click an empty line, or press Enter for a new one.
Type / to open the block menu.
Keep typing to filter, then choose a block and press Enter.
Block families
Text — paragraph, headings, bulleted and numbered lists, code block.
Media — image, video, audio, PDF, web embed, link preview.
Interactive — quiz, code playground, magic (AI) block, math equation, flip card, scenarios, H5P.
Layout — info and warning callouts, badge, table, divider.
Arrange and format
Hover a block to reveal its handle; drag the handle to move it.
The block menu offers duplicate, delete and block-specific options.
Select text for bold, italic, links and inline code.
Write together in real time
When co-authors open the same page you see each other's cursors, and changes merge automatically.
The editor also has an AI panel for drafting and improving content — see AI tools for teaching.
Wait for the save indicator
Content saves as you edit. Wait for the save indicator before closing the tab.

title: Video & AI captions
summary: Upload or embed video, and generate captions — and translations — for hosted videos with AI.
text:
Video activities host a file you upload or embed a YouTube video. For hosted videos, ValidBridge can generate captions with AI and translate them.
In the new-video dialog, or when editing a hosted video, find AI Closed Captions.
Turn on Generate with AI.
Pick the spoken language, or leave it on Auto-detect.
Choose the caption languages (including custom codes such as sw for Swahili).
Click Generate captions. Each language moves through queued → processing → ready, then appears in the player's CC menu.
Generation runs in the background, and long videos work just like short ones.
Uses AI credits
Cost scales with video length and number of languages. If AI is off or credits have run out, you are told before anything is charged.

Review important captions
AI transcription can get names and technical terms wrong.

title: Working through a course
summary: The activity view, marking activities complete, resuming where you left off, and leaving a course.
text:
A course shows its chapters and activities alongside the activity you are on. Follow the order or jump around.
Chapter list — completed activities are marked so you can see what is left.
Content area — the page, video, PDF or assignment itself.
Next / Previous — move through the course in order.
Ask AI — opens the Copilot with this activity in context (see Ask AI).
Live lessons — upcoming and live classes for this course, and recordings of past ones.
Completing activities
Most activities complete when you finish them and use the completion control. Assignments complete when you submit them. A course is complete when every required activity is done.
Pick up where you left off
Open the course from My learning to jump back to where you were.

Leaving a course
From My learning you can remove a course from your Trail. This clears your progress for it.

title: Activity types explained
summary: Dynamic pages, video, documents, assignments and SCORM — what each looks like and how it completes.
text:
TypeWhat you seeHow it completes
Dynamic pageRich content: text, images, code, quizzes, callouts and embeds.Read to the end and confirm.
VideoA hosted or YouTube video, sometimes with AI captions. Live lesson recordings are videos too.Watch and confirm.
DocumentA PDF in a built-in viewer.Read and confirm.
AssignmentGradable tasks — file upload, quiz, short answer, number, code, form or custom.Submit your work.
SCORMAn embedded SCORM 1.2 / 2004 package.Tracked by the package.

Interactive pages
Quizzes and flip cards give instant feedback.
A Code Playground lets you write and run code — see Code exercises.
Scenarios let you choose a path and see the outcome.

title: What is LiveBridge?
summary: LiveBridge is the live classroom built into every course. Lecturers and students meet in the browser — no separate meeting app or link-sharing needed.
text:
LiveBridge is ValidBridge's live classroom. A live lesson belongs to a course: the lecturer schedules it from the course, students join it from the same course, and everything that happens — attendance, questions, poll and quiz answers, the recording — stays with that course. Nobody has to leave ValidBridge or install anything; it runs in the browser on desktop, tablet and phone.
What you can do in a live lesson
Talk on camera and microphone, and share your screen (lecturers).
Chat with the class, and ask the lecturer questions in a dedicated Q&A.
Run quick polls and live quizzes built from the course's own quizzes.
Raise a hand and send reactions (students).
Record the lesson — the recording is added to the course as a video lesson.
Review attendance and participation for every student afterwards.
Who can do what
In the classroomWhoCan
LecturerAnyone who can edit the course (owner, contributors, instructors, admins)Schedule and start lessons, share screen, record, launch polls and quizzes, moderate participants, end the lesson, see attendance.
StudentLearners with access to the courseJoin, chat, ask questions, vote, answer quizzes, raise a hand, react, and use mic and camera unless the lecturer turns them off.

Where to start
Lecturers: Schedule a live lesson, then start and teach it.
Students: Join a live lesson.

title: Schedule a live lesson
summary: Create a live lesson from a course, choose its time, and decide whether it is recorded and whether recordings go straight to students.
text:
Live lessons are scheduled per course. You need permission to edit the course.
Open the course and find the Live lessons panel, then click Schedule. (Or in the dashboard, open the course, go to its LiveBridge tab and click Schedule a live lesson.)
Enter a Lesson title, the Starts at date and time, and an optional description.
Choose the recording options (see below), then click Schedule lesson.
Students enrolled in the course see the lesson in the course's Live lessons panel and under Live lessons in their sidebar, and can join as soon as you go live.
Recording options
Record automatically — recording starts as soon as the lesson goes live. You can also start and stop recording by hand during the lesson.
Publish recordings to students — when on, the finished recording is published to the course straight away. When off, it is added as a draft lesson for you to review and publish yourself.
Recording availability
Recording controls only appear when recording is enabled for your ValidBridge workspace. If you do not see them, contact support.

Next: invite students or start the lesson.

title: Invite students to a live lesson
summary: Share the lesson link, email every enrolled student or specific addresses, or add the lesson to Google Calendar.
text:
Every live lesson has its own link. Click Invite next to a lesson — in the course's Live lessons panel or in the LiveBridge tab — to share it.
Share link
Copy lesson link or Copy joining info (title, time and link) to paste into a message.
Add to Google Calendar creates a calendar event with the link.
Email
Switch to the Email tab.
Tick All enrolled students, and/or paste other email addresses (separated by commas, spaces or new lines — up to 100 per send).
Add an optional personal note, then click Send invitations.
Only people with course access can join
Anyone opening the link must sign in. People who can see the course but have not enrolled get an Enroll & join button. For paid courses they need to buy access first.

title: Start and teach a live lesson
summary: Check your devices, start the lesson, share your screen, choose what students see and record the class.
text:
Start the lesson
Open the lesson — click Open in the course's Live lessons panel, or Open classroom in the LiveBridge tab.
On the device check screen, test your microphone and camera. Lecturers start with both on; use Settings to pick a different microphone, camera or speaker.
Click Start lesson. The lesson goes live and students can join immediately. (Once it has started, the button reads Enter classroom.)
The control bar
ControlWhat it does
Microphone / CameraTurn your audio and video on or off.
Share screenPresent a screen, window or browser tab. Click Stop sharing to finish.
Start / Stop recordingRecord the lesson (shown when recording is available). A REC badge tells everyone the lesson is being recorded.
SettingsChoose microphone, camera and speaker.
PanelsOpen Chat, Q&A, Polls, Quiz, People, Info and Attendance.
LeaveLeave the lesson (it keeps running) or end it for everyone.

Choose what students see
While you share your screen, a What students see switch appears on the stage. Choose Presentation to put your shared screen in focus, or Camera to put your video first.
Use headphones
Headphones prevent echo when several people have their microphones on. If the connection weakens, LiveBridge lowers video quality automatically and the lesson keeps going.

title: Chat, Q&A, polls and live quizzes
summary: Keep students involved: answer questions, launch quick polls, and run a quiz from the course’s existing quiz questions.
text:
Chat
Messages in Chat are visible to everyone in the lesson.
Q&A
Students ask the lecturer questions in the Q&A panel; questions are shared with the class. Lecturers can Reply with an answer for everyone, mark a question Answered, Dismiss it, or Reopen it. Filter by Open, Answered or All.
Polls
Open Polls and choose Launch a poll.
Type the question and at least two options (Add option for more).
Optionally set a Time limit, then click Launch poll.
Students vote from a prompt on their screen and see results after voting. Click Close poll when done.
Live quizzes
Live quizzes reuse the questions you already wrote: any quiz task in an assignment or quiz block in a lesson of this course can be run live.
Open the Quiz panel and Choose a quiz (assignment quiz or lesson quiz).
Set the Time per question and click Start quiz.
Students answer each question on their own screen. When the time runs out, everyone sees the correct answer and how the class did. Click Next question to continue.
After the last question, click Show results for the class summary. You can stop early at any time with End quiz.
Scores count
Live quiz answers and poll votes are saved and appear in the lesson report and in each student's engagement figures.

For students: hands and reactions
Use Raise hand to get the lecturer's attention (they see a Hands raised list) and React to send a quick emoji.

title: Manage participants
summary: Mute students, turn off their microphone and camera access, lower hands, or remove someone from the lesson.
text:
Open the People panel to see lecturers, students and anyone with a raised hand. Search by name, then open a participant's actions:
Lower hand — clear a raised hand.
Mute microphone / Stop camera — switch off their audio or video once; they can turn it back on.
Turn off mic & camera access — stops them using microphone and camera for the rest of the lesson, until you choose Allow mic & camera.
Remove from lesson — disconnects them; they cannot rejoin this lesson.
Removal is final for that lesson
A removed student cannot come back into the same live lesson. Use mute or media access for everyday classroom management.

title: End a lesson and find the recording
summary: End the lesson for everyone, then find the recording as a video lesson inside the course.
text:
Ending the lesson
Click Leave in the control bar.
Choose End lesson for everyone and confirm. Everyone is disconnected and the lesson is marked finished. (Leave lesson instead lets the lesson continue without you.)
Where the recording goes
After a recorded lesson, the recording is processed and then added to the course as a video activity — next to the lesson's linked activity, otherwise in the course's last chapter, or in a Live lesson recordings chapter. Its status moves from Processing to Ready.
If Publish recordings to students was on, students can watch it right away.
Otherwise it is a Draft: open the lesson report and click Review draft, check it, then publish it like any other activity.
Students find recordings under Recorded lessons in the course's Live lessons panel (Watch) and under Catch up on recordings on their Live lessons page.

title: Attendance and live lesson reports
summary: See who attended, who was late or left early, how students took part, and poll and quiz results — per lesson and per student.
text:
During the lesson
Lecturers have an Attendance panel showing who is here now, who has attended and the average attendance so far.
After the lesson
In the dashboard, open the course and its LiveBridge tab (or click Live lesson reports on the course page).
Lessons — every live lesson with its status, attendees, time attended, questions, quiz average and recording. Click View report for one lesson.
Lesson report — attendees and attendance rate, time attended, late and early leavers, participation (messages, questions, poll votes, quiz answers, raised hands), each poll and live quiz, recordings, and a row per student.
Learner engagement — every enrolled student's course progress, assignments and quizzes next to their live attendance and participation.
Attendance statuses
StatusMeaning
PresentAttended the lesson on time.
LateJoined after the start.
Left earlyLeft before the lesson ended.
PartialAttended only part of the lesson.
AbsentEnrolled but did not join.

Admins can also see a student's live lessons in their individual analytics — see Analytics for a single learner.

title: Join a live lesson (students)
summary: Join from the course or your Live lessons page. You join with microphone and camera off and can turn them on any time.
text:
Find the lesson: a Live now banner appears while one of your lessons is live, the Live lessons item in your sidebar shows a Live badge, and each course lists its lessons in a Live lessons panel. You can also open a link your lecturer sent.
Click Join now (or Enter classroom).
On the device check screen, optionally turn on your microphone or camera, then click Join lesson.
Early?
If the lecturer has not started yet you will see The lesson hasn't started yet. Keep the page open — it updates automatically when the lesson goes live.

Access rules
You must be signed in and have access to the course.
If you can see the course but are not enrolled, use Enroll & join.
For a paid course, get access from the course page first — see Paying for a course.
All your upcoming lessons and past recordings are on your Live lessons page.

title: LiveBridge troubleshooting
summary: Microphone or camera blocked, “Reconnecting…”, joined from another tab, removed from a lesson and other common live-class issues.
text:
My microphone or camera is blocked
Your browser has denied access. Allow the microphone and camera in the browser's site settings (the lock or camera icon in the address bar), then try again. If the device is “in use by another app”, close that app.

The microphone or camera button is disabled
The lecturer has turned off microphone and camera for you in this lesson. They can allow it again from the People panel.

I see “Reconnecting…”
Your connection dropped briefly. Wait — the lesson resumes automatically. If you see Connection lost, check your internet and click Rejoin lesson.

“You joined from somewhere else”
The lesson was opened in another tab or device, so this one disconnected. Click Use this tab instead to continue here.

“Enrollment required” or “part of a paid course”
Enrol in the course (or buy access for a paid course) from the course page, then join again.

I can’t share my screen
Screen sharing is for lecturers, and some phone browsers do not support it. On a computer, allow screen capture when the browser asks.

Others hear an echo
Use headphones, or mute when you are not speaking.

title: Finding & enrolling in courses
summary: Where courses are listed, how to enrol in a free course, and what happens with paid courses.
text:
Organization home — the landing page — the course catalogue, or a custom page your organization designed.
Courses — the full catalogue, from Courses in the sidebar.
Collections — named groups of courses, such as a learning path.
Marketplace — paid offers, with prices, when your organization sells courses.
Enrol in a course
Find the course in the catalogue, a collection, search or the marketplace.
Open it to see its description, chapters and live lessons.
Click Enrol (or Start learning). Free courses open instantly; paid courses take you to checkout — see Paying for a course.
The course is added to My learning and the first activity opens.
Can’t find a course?
It may still be a draft, or restricted to a user group you are not in. Ask your instructor or an admin.

title: Your Trail, progress & certificates
summary: Track every course you have started, your results, and the certificates you have earned.
text:
Your Trail is created the first time you start a course and updates as you work.
Every course you have started, with a completion bar.
Completed activities, and your assignment and quiz results.
Your live lessons, and certificates you have earned.
Open it from My learning in the sidebar or go to your Trail.
Certificates
If a course issues certificates, one is generated when you complete every required activity. Each has a unique identifier so others can verify it, and you can view or share it from your Trail.

title: Add and manage users
summary: Add people, change their role, review signups and deactivate accounts from the Users area.
text:
Add people
In the dashboard, go to Users → Add Member.
Enter the person's email (and name if you have it).
Choose their role.
If signup is open, people can also join themselves — see Signups & user groups.
The Users area
TabWhat it does
UsersEveryone in the organization. Search, open a profile, change roles, deactivate.
User GroupsGroups used to give access to restricted courses and resources.
RolesThe permission matrix.
SignupsPeople waiting for approval to join.
Add MemberCreate an account directly.
Sign-in MethodsWhich sign-in options are allowed, including Google and SSO.
Two-Factor PolicyRequire two-factor authentication for members.
Audit LogsA record of security and admin actions.

Deactivating a user
Open a user's profile to change their role or deactivate them. Deactivated users cannot sign in, but their submissions and progress are kept.
Good to know
To give a student access to a course, enrol them or add them to a user group the course is restricted to.
To invite enrolled students to a live class, use the lesson's Invite button.

title: Signups & user groups
summary: Choose how people join (open or invite-only), add signup fields, and use user groups to control access.
text:
How people join
Open signup — anyone can create an account and join.
Invite-only — only people you invite can join.
With open signup you can add custom signup fields and require approval of new accounts from the Signups tab.
User groups
A user group is a named set of people — a cohort, a class, a department. Restrict a course to a group and only its members can see it. When someone buys an offer linked to a payment group, they can be added to a matching user group automatically (see Payment groups).
Go to Users → User Groups and create a group.
Add members.
On a course's Access & Pricing tab, restrict it to the group.

title: Complete and submit an assignment
summary: Task types you may meet, how autosave and submission work, deadlines, retries and formative assignments.
text:
An assignment is a gradable activity made of one or more tasks.
File upload — attach a document, image or archive.
Quiz — multiple-choice questions, scored automatically.
Short answer — a text answer, sometimes auto-graded against an answer key.
Number answer — a numeric value checked against an expected answer.
Code — code run against test cases.
Form — a structured form defined by your instructor.
Submit
Open the assignment from the course.
Complete each task. Your work autosaves, so you can come back later.
Click Submit. If retries are allowed you can resubmit before the deadline.
Once graded, open the assignment to see your score and feedback per task.
Deadlines
If a due date is set, the assignment closes when it passes — you are warned before saving stops. Late submissions are flagged to the instructor.
Formative assignments
Formative assignments have no score. Handing in your work unlocks a model answer so you can compare and self-assess.
Submission statuses
Not submitted → Pending (saved, not handed in) → Submitted → Late (if past the deadline) → Graded.

title: Create and grade assignments
summary: Build an assignment from tasks, set deadlines and retries, choose a grading scale, and review submissions.
text:
Create an assignment
Add an Assignment activity to a chapter, or open Assignments in the dashboard.
Give it a title, description and optional due date.
Add tasks in the Task Editor; each can have its own instructions and points.
Set the grading scale, whether retries are allowed, and graded or formative mode.
Publish it with the course.
Task types
TaskLearner doesGrading
File uploadAttaches files.Manual
QuizAnswers multiple-choice questions.Automatic
Short answerTypes a text answer.Automatic against an answer key, or manual
Number answerEnters a number.Automatic, with a tolerance
CodeWrites code run against test cases.Automatic
FormFills in a form you define.Manual or automatic

Grading scales
Numeric — a raw score, such as 87 / 100.
Percentage — a score out of 100%.
Alphabet — letter grades, A–F.
Review submissions
Open the assignment and go to Submissions.
Filter by student or task; each row shows its status.
Open a submission. Automatic tasks are already scored; grade manual ones.
Finalise the grade — it is recorded in the learner's Trail.
Formative (ungraded) assignments
Turn on Formative — no grading. Instead of a grade you write a model answer (optionally with a document) and choose when it unlocks: Never, On hand-in or After grading.
Reuse quiz questions live
Quiz tasks can also be run as a live quiz during a LiveBridge lesson — see Live quizzes.

title: Quiz blocks, quiz tasks and live quizzes
summary: The three kinds of quiz in ValidBridge and when to use each one.
text:
KindWhere it livesGraded?
Quiz blockInside a dynamic page (insert it from the editor’s / menu).No — a quick knowledge check with instant feedback.
Quiz taskInside an assignment.Yes — scored automatically and saved as a submission.
Live quizRun during a LiveBridge lesson from a quiz block or quiz task.Scored per question; results appear in the lesson report.

Write your questions once: any quiz block or quiz task in a course can be run live in that course's lessons. See Chat, Q&A, polls and live quizzes.
Live quizzes need auto-scorable questions
A live quiz only uses questions that can be scored automatically. If a quiz has none, LiveBridge tells you it cannot be run.

title: Code exercises
summary: Write and run code in the browser against your instructor’s test cases, in 30 languages.
text:
A Code Playground block gives you an in-browser editor. Write a solution, then run it against the test cases your instructor defined.
Choose the language (the exercise usually preselects it).
Write your solution.
Click Run. Each test case reports pass or fail, with time and memory used.
Fix and re-run until every test passes. Your submission is saved.
Code runs in an isolated sandbox. Thirty languages are supported, including Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, Rust, Go, C#, Ruby, PHP, SQL and Bash.
A Code Playground block in a page is practice.
A Code task in an assignment counts towards that assignment's grade.

title: How payments work
summary: Learners pay through Paystack. Get paid straight to your bank with just your bank details, or connect your own Paystack account.
text:
Payments in ValidBridge run on Paystack. Learners pay on Paystack's secure checkout page. You choose how you get paid:
Get paid to M-PESA or your bank (recommended) — no Paystack account needed. Enter your M-PESA, till, Airtel Money or bank details once and Paystack pays each sale straight to you.
Use your own Paystack account — if you already have one, connect it with your API keys and the money settles into it.
The flow at a glance
An admin connects Paystack under Payments → Configuration.
You create offers — a price (one-time or subscription) linked to courses or a payment group.
A learner clicks Get access or Subscribe and pays on Paystack.
Paystack notifies ValidBridge, which unlocks the courses for that learner immediately.
What learners can pay with
Whatever your Paystack account accepts — typically cards, bank payments and mobile money such as M-Pesa, depending on your country and Paystack settings.
Payments tabWhat it is for
OverviewEvery customer, the offer they bought, amount, status and since when.
OffersThe things you sell: price, type and the courses they unlock.
Payment GroupsBundles of courses sold together, optionally mirrored into a user group.
ConfigurationChoose how you get paid: your bank details, or your own Paystack keys.

Turn the feature on first
Payments must be enabled for your organization. If you do not see Payments in the dashboard, check the features in Organization settings or contact support.

title: Set up how you get paid
summary: Get paid to M-PESA, a till, Airtel Money or a bank (no Paystack account needed), or connect your own Paystack account.
text:
Go to Payments → Configuration (you need the Admin role) and pick one of the two options.
Option A: Get paid to M-PESA or your bank
The quickest way. You do not need a Paystack account.
Click Get paid to M-PESA or your bank.
Choose how you are paid: M-PESA (a phone number), M-PESA Till (a Buy Goods till number), Bank account or Airtel Money.
Enter the number and the name on the account, then click Continue.
Check the summary carefully and click Yes, start accepting payments.
Double-check the number
In Kenya, Paystack cannot look up the account holder's name, so a mistyped number would send your money to someone else. The summary step is there to catch this.

Verification before the first payout
You can start selling as soon as you save. Before the first payout, ValidBridge confirms your payout details; until then the page shows Verifying your payout details and your earnings are held safely. Once verified, each sale is paid out automatically, usually within one or two business days. If you change your payout details, they are verified again.
ValidBridge takes 0% of your sales. Paystack's processing fee is added on top for the learner — they choose Pay with M-PESA or Pay with card and see the exact total — so you receive your full price. Subscriptions are paid by card. M-PESA Paybill numbers are not supported yet — use a till, phone or bank account.
Option B: Use your own Paystack account
In the Paystack Dashboard (dashboard.paystack.com), open Settings → API Keys & Webhooks and copy your secret key (sk_live_ or sk_test_) and, optionally, your public key.
In ValidBridge, click I already have a Paystack account, paste the keys and click Connect. ValidBridge checks them with Paystack before saving, and tells you if a key is wrong or if you mixed test and live keys.
In the same Paystack settings page, set the Webhook URL to your ValidBridge API address followed by /api/v1/payments/paystack/webhook. ValidBridge uses it to hear about renewals, cancellations and refunds.
Test with your sk_test_ key and Paystack's test cards first, then click Update keys and switch to your live key (and the live webhook URL).
Switching or turning off
You can switch between the two options at any time from the same page.
Turn off stops new sales. Learners who already paid keep their access.
Your details are protected
Secret keys are encrypted before they are stored and are only used by the ValidBridge server. Only the last four digits of your bank account are kept on ValidBridge.

title: Create an offer
summary: Set a one-time or subscription price (fixed or pay-what-you-want), choose the currency, and link the courses it unlocks.
text:
An offer is something learners can buy.
Open Payments → Offers and create a new offer.
Enter an Offer Name, description and optional benefits (comma-separated).
Choose the Offer Type: one-time or subscription. For subscriptions, pick a Billing Interval — monthly or yearly.
Choose the Price Type: a fixed price, or customer's choice (pay what you want, with your amount as the minimum).
Set the amount and Currency (KES by default). Use a currency your Paystack account supports.
Under Access, add courses directly and/or link a payment group.
Save. Public offers appear in your marketplace.
Subscriptions create a Paystack plan
When you save a subscription offer, ValidBridge creates (or updates) the matching plan in your Paystack account automatically. Connect Paystack before creating subscription offers.

Use Preview Shop at the top of the Payments pages to see your marketplace as learners do.

title: Payment groups (bundles)
summary: Sell several courses together, and mirror buyers into a user group so they get access everywhere.
text:
A payment group is a bundle of courses. Link an offer to a group and buying the offer unlocks every course in it — add a course to the group later and existing buyers get it too.
Open Payments → Payment Groups and create a group with a name and description.
Add the courses it contains.
Link one or more offers to the group (in each offer's Access section).
Optionally click Sync to mirror the group into a user group: buyers become members while their purchase is active and are removed if it is cancelled or refunded.
Why sync?
A synced user group lets paying learners reach everything the user group unlocks — course listings, communities and certificates — not just the paywalled pages.

title: Paying for a course (learners)
summary: Buy a course or subscribe on Paystack's secure checkout, then find your purchases and payment history in your account.
text:
Open the course, or the offer in the marketplace.
Click the button for how you want to pay — for example Pay with M-PESA or Pay with card (subscriptions are paid by card). Each button shows the exact total, including the small payment processing fee for that method. For pay-what-you-want offers, enter an amount at or above the minimum first. Sign in if asked.
You are taken to Paystack's secure checkout to complete the payment.
You return to ValidBridge and the course unlocks as soon as Paystack confirms the payment — usually within seconds.
Your purchases and receipts
Account → Purchases — the courses and subscriptions you have bought.
Account → Billing — active subscriptions with the next payment date, and your payment history.
Who you are paying
You pay the organization that runs the course, through Paystack. For refunds or questions about a charge, contact that organization.

title: Subscriptions, cancellations & refunds
summary: How subscriptions renew, what happens when a learner cancels or a payment fails, and how refunds work.
text:
Renewals
Subscriptions are billed by Paystack every month or year. Each successful renewal keeps access active; a failed renewal suspends access until a later payment succeeds.
Cancelling
Learners cancel from Account → Billing (click Cancel next to the subscription). Billing stops in Paystack and access ends immediately — there is no grace period.
Refunds
If you use your own Paystack account, issue refunds from your Paystack Dashboard (use the Paystack Dashboard button on the Payments pages). If you get paid through ValidBridge, contact ValidBridge support to refund a sale. When Paystack reports the refund, ValidBridge marks the purchase refunded and removes the access it granted.
Payouts
If you get paid through ValidBridge (M-PESA, till, Airtel Money or bank), Paystack pays each sale into the account you entered — your full price, because learners pay the processing fee on top — once your payout details are verified. If you use your own Paystack account, the money settles into it on Paystack's schedule and fees.
Purchase statuses
StatusMeaning
PendingCheckout started but not yet paid.
CompletedOne-time purchase paid — access granted.
ActiveSubscription paid and current — access granted.
CancelledSubscription cancelled — access ended.
FailedA subscription payment failed — access suspended.
RefundedPayment refunded — access removed.

title: Payments troubleshooting
summary: Checkout unavailable, paid but still locked, subscription offer errors and other payment questions.
text:
Learners see no checkout button
Payments may be switched off for the organization, Paystack may not be connected, or the offer is not public. Check Payments → Configuration and the offer settings.

A learner paid but the course is still locked
ValidBridge checks the payment with Paystack as soon as the learner returns from checkout, and again when Paystack's webhook arrives. If the learner closed the page early and you use your own Paystack account, check the webhook URL in your Paystack settings (see Set up how you get paid) and that the key mode (test or live) matches. The purchase shows as Pending in Payments → Overview until it is confirmed.

“Cannot create a subscription without credentials configured”
Subscription offers need a Paystack plan, so connect Paystack before saving the offer.

“Amount must be at least …”
On a pay-what-you-want offer the amount entered is below the minimum price.

title: Organization analytics
summary: Engagement, course and growth metrics for the whole organization over 7, 30 or 90 days.
text:
Open Analytics in the dashboard (under Insights) to see how the whole organization is used. Switch between 7, 30 and 90 day windows.
User engagement — activity views, time spent and interaction patterns.
Courses — the most popular courses and how learners progress through them.
Organization — overall usage and growth.
The Overview tab covers the essentials; Advanced adds deeper reporting.
Recent activity can lag
Analytics data is cached for speed, so the last few minutes of activity may take a little while to appear.

title: Course analytics
summary: Views, completion, drop-off points and assessment results for a single course.
text:
Each course has an Analytics tab in the dashboard showing:
Activity views and completion over time.
Where learners stop or drop off.
Assignment and quiz performance.
Use it to find activities that need a clearer explanation. For live classes, the course's LiveBridge tab has attendance and participation — see Attendance and live lesson reports.

title: Analytics for a single learner
summary: Open one student’s full record — courses, assignments, code, community, certificates, live lessons and behaviour — or compare and export several.
text:
In the dashboard, go to Users.
Click Analytics on a student's row to open their record, or open the full analytics page.
Browse the tabs: connections, courses, assignments, code, community, certificates, LiveBridge (live lessons attended, attendance, live quiz scores and interactions) and behaviour.
Compare and export
Select several students in the list to Compare analytics side by side, or Export their analytics for reporting.

title: Organization settings
summary: Name, features, branding, menu, landing page, AI, usage and the danger zone — what each settings tab controls.
text:
Open Organization in the dashboard sidebar.
TabWhat it controls
GeneralName, slug, description, and which features are enabled.
BrandingLogo, favicon, colours and font.
MenuLinks in the learner sidebar and top navigation.
LandingA custom landing page for the organization home.
AITurn AI on or off, cap requests per user, and toggle AI surfaces.
UsagePlan usage and limits.
OtherAdditional options such as signup and integrations.
Danger zoneIrreversible actions such as deleting the organization.

Feature toggles
Communities, podcasts, boards, playgrounds, payments, the library, analytics and other features are enabled per organization. A feature that is off disappears from the sidebar for everyone.
The danger zone is permanent
Deleting an organization removes its courses, users and data. Export what you need first.

title: Branding & the landing page
summary: Make the workspace your own: logo, colour and font, the learner menu, and a custom landing page.
text:
Branding
Upload a logo and favicon, pick a primary colour and choose a font. The colour and font apply across your organization.
Menu
From Menu, reorder, rename or add links (including external URLs) in the learner sidebar and top navigation.
Landing page
By default the organization home is a course catalogue. From Landing you can build a custom page with sections and calls to action instead.
Start with three changes
A logo, a primary colour and a font make the platform feel like yours.

title: Roles & permissions
summary: The permission matrix behind each role, and how to create custom roles.
text:
A role is a per-resource permission matrix covering courses, users, user groups, collections, the organization, chapters, activities, roles, the dashboard, communities, discussions, podcasts, boards and playgrounds. The four default roles are described in Accounts, roles & permissions.
Create a custom role
Go to Users → Roles.
Create a role and name it.
Toggle permissions per resource — e.g. allow editing course content but not managing access.
Assign the role to people from the Users tab.
Least privilege
Give people the narrowest role that lets them do their job. A content writer does not need payments or user management.

Course editors run live lessons
Anyone who can edit a course can schedule and run its LiveBridge lessons and see their reports.

title: The Developers area at a glance
summary: What each Developers page does — API access, automations, domains, SEO and SSO — which plan it needs, and where the full guides are.
text:
The Developers entry in the dashboard sidebar connects ValidBridge to your school's other systems. Each page has its own step-by-step guide:
PageWhat it is forPlan
API AccessTokens for your own software to sync students, enrolments and progress.Pro and above
AutomationsSend events to your systems, Zapier, Make or n8n.Pro and above
DomainsServe your organization on your own address.Pro and above
SEOHow you appear in search results and when shared.Standard and above
SSOSign in with the school’s identity provider.Enterprise

Everything is in the Integrations & developer tools topic.

title: API access & tokens
summary: Create, scope and revoke API tokens, authenticate requests, and use the API to sync students, enrolments and progress with your own systems.
text:
API tokens let your own software — a student information system, an admissions portal, a reporting script — work with your ValidBridge organization without a person signing in. Each token belongs to one organization.
Who can use it
API access is available on the Pro plan and above. Creating and managing tokens needs the Admin role.

Create a token
In the dashboard, open Developers → API Access (open API Access).
On the API Tokens tab, click Create Token.
Give it a Token Name that says what uses it (for example “SIS nightly sync”) and, optionally, a description.
Optionally set an Expiration Date. Leave it empty for a token that never expires.
Choose its Permissions (see below) and create it.
Copy the token straight away and store it in your password manager or secrets store. It is shown only once. Tokens start with vb_.
Permissions
Read Only — the token can read but not change anything. The safe default.
Full Access — create, read, update and delete on every resource.
Custom — tick create, read, update or delete per resource: courses, activities, assignments, chapters, folders, media, certifications, user groups and payments, plus search.
Give each integration its own token with the narrowest permissions it needs, so you can revoke one without breaking the others.
Authenticate requests
Send the token in the Authorization header of every request, as a bearer token:
Authorization: Bearer vb_your_token_here

Requests and responses are JSON. The Documentation & Playground tab on the same page lists every endpoint with its full address, parameters and example responses, lets you try calls with your token, and gives you a ready-to-copy curl command.
What you can do with it
The school-administration part of the API is built for syncing with your own systems. All of it is scoped to your organization's slug (the name in your ValidBridge address). The most useful calls:
TaskRequest
Create (provision) a student or staff accountPOST /admin/{org_slug}/users
Find a user by emailGET /admin/{org_slug}/users/by-email/{email}
Enrol a user in a coursePOST /admin/{org_slug}/enrollments/{user_id}/{course_uuid}
Enrol many users at oncePOST /admin/{org_slug}/enrollments/bulk
Read a user’s progress in all coursesGET /admin/{org_slug}/progress/{user_id}
List a user’s certificatesGET /admin/{org_slug}/certifications/{user_id}
Add a user to a user group (class, stream)POST /admin/{org_slug}/usergroups/{usergroup_uuid}/members/{user_id}
Send a user a one-click sign-in link from your portalPOST /admin/{org_slug}/auth/magic-link

Paths are relative to the API address shown in the playground. The playground is the reference: it is always up to date with what your plan allows.
Admin and staff accounts are protected
A token cannot sign in as, or issue sign-in links for, an organization Admin or Maintainer.

Limits
Creating or regenerating tokens: 10 per hour.
Provisioning users: 30 per minute per token.
Looking users up by email: 60 per minute per token.
Over a limit, the API answers 429 Too Many Requests. Wait and retry, and spread large imports out or use the bulk enrolment call.
Revoke or regenerate a token
The token list shows each token's prefix, status, when it was last used and when it expires. From a token's actions:
Regenerate issues a new secret for the same token and settings. The old secret stops working immediately, so update your integration at once.
Revoke switches the token off for good. Use it when an integration is retired or a token may have leaked.
Treat tokens like passwords
Never put a token in a web page, a mobile app, a shared spreadsheet or an email. Keep it on a server you control. A token that never expires is convenient but riskier — set an expiry and rotate it on a schedule if you can.

title: Automations & webhooks
summary: Send events such as enrolments, completions and grades to your systems, Zapier, Make or n8n, and verify each delivery with its signing secret.
text:
A webhook sends a message to an address you choose the moment something happens in your organization — a learner enrols, completes a course, submits an assignment or earns a certificate. Use it to update your own records or to start a workflow in Zapier, Make or n8n.
Who can use it
Automations are available on the Pro plan and above, for admins.

Add an endpoint
Go to Developers → Automations (open Automations) and add an endpoint.
Paste the Endpoint URL that should receive events. It must be a public https:// address.
Add a description so others know what it is for.
Tick the events you want. Each event shows an example of the data it sends.
Click Create Endpoint and copy the Signing Secret. It is shown only once.
Use Send test event to send a ping and check it arrives.
Connect Zapier, Make or n8n
In your automation tool, start a workflow with its “catch webhook” trigger (in Zapier: Webhooks by Zapier → Catch Hook). Copy the address it gives you into the Endpoint URL above, send a test event, and build the rest of the workflow from the sample data.
Events you can subscribe to
GroupEvents
Learning progressCourse enrolled, activity completed, course completed, assignment submitted, assignment graded, certificate claimed, certificate revoked
Users & accessUser signed up, email verified, role changed, invited, removed from the organization
Courses & contentCourse created, published or unpublished, deleted, announcement posted; contributors added or removed; folders and podcast episodes
Community & collaborationDiscussions and comments, pins, locks and votes; new boards and playgrounds
Groups & subscriptionsUser groups created or deleted, members or courses added; subscription packs activated or cancelled
OrganizationSign-up method, AI settings or payment settings changed

The endpoint page shows the exact event names and sample data for each one.
What a delivery looks like
Each event is an HTTP POST with a JSON body:
Example body
{
 "event": "course_enrolled",
 "delivery_id": "dlv_3f9c1a7e5b2d4c80",
 "timestamp": "2026-09-24T08:15:02Z",
 "org_id": 42,
 "data": {
 "user": { "user_uuid": "user_…", "email": "amina@school.ac.ke", "username": "amina" },
 "course": { "course_uuid": "course_…", "name": "Form 3 Chemistry" }
 }
}

X-Webhook-Event — the event name.
X-Webhook-Delivery — a unique delivery id. Store it and ignore repeats, so a retried delivery is only processed once.
X-Webhook-Signature — sha256= followed by an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, made with your signing secret.
Verify the signature
Before trusting a delivery, recompute the signature from the raw body (before any JSON parsing) and compare it with the header. Reject anything that does not match.
Python
import hmac, hashlib

def is_from_validbridge(raw_body: bytes, signature_header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
 expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
 return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature_header or "")

Node.js
const crypto = require('crypto')

function isFromValidBridge(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret) {
 const expected = 'sha256=' + crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')
 const a = Buffer.from(expected)
 const b = Buffer.from(signatureHeader || '')
 return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b)
}

Retries and delivery logs
Answer with any 2xx status within 10 seconds to confirm receipt.
Otherwise the delivery is retried, up to 3 attempts in total, a few seconds apart. Redirects are not followed.
View delivery logs shows each attempt with its status code and the start of your response — the first place to look when something is missing. The most recent 200 attempts per endpoint are kept.
Manage endpoints
Edit the URL, description or events at any time.
Disable an endpoint to pause deliveries without losing its settings.
Regenerate the secret if it may have leaked. The old secret stops working immediately; update your receiver first.
Delete an endpoint you no longer need.

title: Use your own domain
summary: Serve your school’s ValidBridge site on an address like learn.school.ac.ke: add the domain, create two DNS records, verify, and HTTPS is set up automatically.
text:
By default your organization lives at its ValidBridge address. With a custom domain, learners visit your own address instead — for example learn.school.ac.ke — with a secure HTTPS certificate issued for you.
Who can use it
Custom domains are available on the Pro plan and above. You need the Admin role in ValidBridge and access to your domain's DNS settings (often held by your IT team or web host).

Pick the right address
Use a subdomain such as learn.school.ac.ke or portal.academy.co.ke. Your main website (school.ac.ke) usually cannot take the CNAME record this needs, and pointing it at ValidBridge would replace your existing site.
1. Add the domain
Go to Developers → Domains (open Domains) and click Add Domain.
Type the full address, e.g. learn.school.ac.ke, and add it.
The domain appears as Pending, and ValidBridge shows the two DNS records to create.
2. Create the DNS records
At your domain registrar or DNS host (KENIC reseller, Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap…), create both records exactly as shown on the page:
TypeName / hostValuePurpose
TXT_validbridge-verification.learnvalidbridge-verify=… (your code)Proves you own the domain
CNAMElearnThe target shown on the pageSends visitors to ValidBridge

The example is for learn.school.ac.ke. The TXT record must end up at _validbridge-verification.learn.school.ac.ke. Most DNS hosts add your domain to the name automatically, so you type only the part before it (_validbridge-verification.learn and learn). If the page shows a longer name than your DNS host expects, keep only the part before your own domain.
Copy, don’t retype
Use the copy buttons on the Domains page. A single wrong character in the code or the CNAME target stops verification.

3. Verify
Wait for the records to take effect — often minutes, occasionally up to 48 hours.
Click Verify next to the domain, then Verify DNS.
When the TXT record is found, the domain changes to Verified.
4. HTTPS is set up for you
Once the domain is verified and the CNAME is in place, a certificate is issued automatically, usually within a few minutes. The SSL column updates on its own; you can also open the domain and click Check.
SSL badgeMeaning
SSL ActiveThe certificate is live. Learners can use the address.
ProvisioningThe certificate is being issued. Give it a few minutes.
InvalidThe certificate could not be issued — almost always because the CNAME is missing or points somewhere else. Fix it, then verify again.
UnknownThe status could not be read right now. Check again shortly.

Removing a domain
Click the delete (bin) icon next to the domain and confirm. The address stops serving your organization and its certificate is released. Then delete the TXT and CNAME records at your DNS host. Your ValidBridge address keeps working throughout.
Troubleshooting
“TXT record not found”
The record is missing, has not spread yet, or sits at the wrong name (often the domain was added twice, e.g. …learn.school.ac.ke.school.ac.ke). Check the name and wait a little before verifying again.

“TXT record found but value doesn’t match”
The value was mistyped or is from an earlier attempt. Copy it again from the Domains page.

Verified, but the certificate stays in Provisioning
Check that the CNAME exists and points to the exact target shown. If your DNS is on Cloudflare, set the record to DNS only (grey cloud) while the certificate is issued. Still stuck after an hour? Email support@validbridge.co.ke with the domain name.

title: Single sign-on (SSO)
summary: Set up SSO so staff and students sign in with the school’s identity provider — Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta and others — through SAML or OpenID Connect.
text:
With SSO, people sign in to ValidBridge with the account they already use at school, managed by your identity provider (IdP). There are two ways to connect:
SAML and managed connections (WorkOS) — the simplest route for Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Google Workspace, Okta, Keycloak, Auth0 or any SAML provider. Your IT team completes a guided setup portal.
Custom OIDC — connect directly to any OpenID Connect provider using a client ID and secret from your IdP.
Who can use it
SSO is an Enterprise plan feature and is set up by an organization admin under Developers → SSO (open SSO).

Option A — SAML via WorkOS
In SSO Provider, choose WorkOS.
Enter your WorkOS Organization ID (it starts with org_). If you do not have one, email support@validbridge.co.ke and we will set it up for your school.
Click Save Configuration.
Click Configure Identity Provider. The setup portal opens and walks your IT team through connecting your IdP step by step — it shows the values to paste into Entra ID, Google or Okta.
Finish the options below and switch on Enable SSO.
Option B — Custom OIDC
First, register ValidBridge as an application (web app) in your IdP:
Set the redirect URI (also called callback URL). It ends in /api/v1/auth/sso/callback; email support@validbridge.co.ke to confirm the exact address for your organization, especially if you use your own domain.
Allow the openid, email and profile scopes.
Copy the application's client ID and create a client secret.
Then, in ValidBridge:
In SSO Provider, choose Custom OIDC.
Issuer URL: your IdP's issuer, e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0 or https://accounts.google.com. Sign-in endpoints are discovered from it automatically.
Paste the Client ID and Client Secret.
Leave Scopes as openid email profile unless your IdP needs more (space-separated).
Finish the options below and click Save Configuration.
Options for both
Allowed Email Domains — a comma-separated list such as school.ac.ke, students.school.ac.ke. Only these addresses can sign in with SSO. Leave it empty to allow any.
Auto-provision Users — create an account automatically the first time someone signs in with SSO. When it is off, only people who already have an account (matched by email) can use SSO.
Enable SSO — shows the SSO button on your sign-in page.
SSO must also be allowed under Users → Sign-in Methods — see Add and manage users.
What people see
On your organization's sign-in page they click Sign in with SSO.
They sign in at your identity provider as usual.
They come back to ValidBridge, see Authenticating…, and land signed in. Existing accounts are matched by email address.
If your organization requires two-factor authentication, it still applies after SSO.
Troubleshooting
The SSO button does not appear
Check that Enable SSO is on, the configuration is saved, and SSO is allowed under Sign-in Methods.

“Your email domain is not allowed for this organization”
The person's address is not in Allowed Email Domains. Add the domain or have them use their school address.

Sign-in fails for someone new
Auto-provision Users is off and they have no account yet. Invite them first, or turn auto-provisioning on.

“Failed to authenticate with the identity provider”
Usually a wrong client secret, an expired secret, or a redirect URI that does not match. Check them in your IdP and in ValidBridge.

Keep a way back in
Before relying on SSO alone, make sure at least one admin can still sign in another way, in case the identity provider is unavailable. Treat the client secret like a password.

title: SEO for your school site
summary: Control how your organization appears in Google and when shared: page titles, descriptions, sharing image, Search Console verification and indexing.
text:
Go to Developers → SEO (open SEO). SEO settings are available on the Standard plan and above.
SettingWhat it does
Title SuffixAdded to every page title, e.g. “ | Riverside Academy”.
Default DescriptionUsed in search results for pages that have no description of their own.
Default OG ImageThe picture shown when a link is shared on WhatsApp, Facebook or X. Use 1200 × 630 pixels.
Twitter HandleYour account, shown on X (Twitter) link cards.
Google Search ConsolePaste the verification code from Search Console to prove you own the site.
Hide ConnectKeep community pages out of search results.

Under Quick Links you will find your sitemap and robots.txt addresses. Submit the sitemap in Google Search Console so new courses are found faster.
Courses have their own SEO
Each course has an SEO tab for its own title, description and image — see Course settings.

Using your own address? Set it up first (Use your own domain) so search engines index the address you want people to remember.

title: Your account settings
summary: Where to change your details, profile, security settings, and see your purchases and billing.
text:
Open your avatar menu and choose Account settings, or go to your account.
TabWhat you can do
GeneralYour name, email and basic account details.
ProfileYour public profile, such as your photo and bio.
SecurityChange your password, set up two-factor authentication, see your current session, or delete your account.
PurchasesCourses and subscriptions you have bought.
BillingActive subscriptions, next payment dates and payment history.

Questions about a purchase? See Paying for a course.

title: Signing in
summary: Email and password, Google, emailed sign-in links and single sign-on — plus resetting a forgotten password.
text:
Depending on what your organization allows, the sign-in page offers:
Email and password — the default.
Google — sign in with your Google account.
Sign in with a link — we email you a secure one-time link. It expires shortly, so use it soon.
Single sign-on (SSO) — sign in through your organization's identity provider.
Forgot your password?
On the sign-in page, click Forgot password?.
Enter your email and click Send Reset Link.
Open the email and choose a new password.
Verify your email
New accounts may need to confirm their email address before signing in. Check your inbox and spam folder for the verification message.

title: Two-factor authentication
summary: Protect your account with a one-time code from an authenticator app, and keep backup codes safe.
text:
Turn it on
Go to Account settings → Security and click Enable under Two-factor authentication.
Confirm your password (skipped if you sign in only with Google or SSO).
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (1Password, Google Authenticator, Authy…), or enter the setup key by hand.
Enter the 6-digit code from the app and click Verify and enable.
Save your backup codes — copy or download them. They are shown only once, and each works once if you lose your phone.
Running low on backup codes?
Generate a new set from the Security tab so you do not get locked out.
Required by your organization?
Admins can require two-factor for everyone (Users → Two-Factor Policy). If so, you will be asked to set it up before continuing.

title: Change your password or delete your account
summary: Update your password, sign out of your session, or permanently delete your account.
text:
Change your password
In Account settings → Security, enter your current password and a new one of at least 8 characters.
Sign out
Use Sign out in your avatar menu, or next to This device in the Security tab.
Delete your account
At the bottom of the Security tab, click Delete account and type your username to confirm.
This cannot be undone
Deleting your account removes it permanently. Cancel any active subscriptions first.

title: Ask AI (the Copilot)
summary: An on-demand tutor that reads the course material you are looking at, cites its sources and suggests follow-ups.
text:
The AI Copilot answers questions using the course material you are studying, so its answers are grounded in your actual lessons.
Open it
From an activity, click Ask AI — it opens in a side drawer with that activity in context.
From anywhere, open the full-page Copilot to ask about all of your courses.
Things to ask
“Explain this activity in simpler terms.”
“Summarise this lesson in five bullet points.”
“Make flashcards from this material.”
“Quiz me on what I have learned so far.”
“Build me a study plan for this course.”
Answers show the sources they used — click one to jump to that activity — and suggest follow-up questions.
Don’t see Ask AI?
AI may be switched off for your organization, or its AI credits may have run out. An admin can check under Organization → AI.

Check important answers
AI can be confidently wrong. Use it as a study aid, not a source of truth.

title: AI tools for teaching
summary: Draft and improve lessons, generate quizzes, images and narrated audio, and build interactive playgrounds.
text:
In the editor
Draft content — write or expand a section from a prompt or outline.
Improve content — clarity, tone and completeness edits you can accept or reject.
Generate quizzes from the material.
Magic block — insert an AI-generated interactive element.
Audio and images
Generate images for activities, and create audio from the Audio block's Generate tab:
Text to speech — narrate text you write.
Podcast (2 voices) — the AI writes a two-host discussion you can edit before generating.
Speak — the AI writes and narrates a single-speaker talk.
Playgrounds
Generate interactive web experiences — simulations, visualisations, widgets — from a prompt, refine them, and choose who can open them.
AI credits
AI features use your organization's AI credits. When credits run low the app lets you know.

Review before publishing
Always check AI-generated content for accuracy and tone before learners see it.

title: Discussions & communities
summary: Post, reply, upvote and react in your organization’s communities; pin, lock and moderate threads.
text:
Communities are spaces for conversation, questions and announcements, separate from course content.
Open Communities in the sidebar (or the communities page).
Pick a community, then open a discussion or start one.
Reply, upvote helpful posts, or add an emoji reaction.
Labels categorise discussions so you can filter them.
Pinned discussions stay at the top.
Locked discussions are read-only.
Moderating
Instructors and admins can pin, lock and delete threads, and manage labels, from the Communities area of the dashboard.

title: Boards
summary: Infinite collaborative whiteboards for group work and workshops, with Owner, Editor and Viewer access.
text:
A board is an infinite canvas several people can edit at once. Changes appear live for everyone.
Draw freehand and add shapes, sticky notes and to-do cards.
Group content in frames.
Drop in cards for web pages, YouTube videos, podcasts, course activities and playgrounds.
Create a board (instructors)
Go to Boards in the dashboard and create a board.
Name it, set a thumbnail, and build the canvas.
Add members as Owner, Editor or Viewer.
Stuck on “connecting”?
Live sync is briefly unavailable. Wait a moment and reload.

title: Podcasts
summary: Publish audio series with episodes; learners listen with a mini-player or any podcast app via RSS.
text:
Listening
Browse Podcasts, open one and press play. A mini-player keeps playing while you move around. Each podcast also has an RSS feed for your favourite podcast app.
Publishing (instructors)
Go to Podcasts in the dashboard and create a podcast with a name, description and cover.
Add episodes and upload their audio.
Reorder episodes to set the listening order.
You can submit the RSS feed to directories such as Apple Podcasts or Spotify yourself; ValidBridge does not publish there for you.

title: Playgrounds (Labs)
summary: Interactive AI-generated simulations and widgets that support a lesson.
text:
Playgrounds are interactive web experiences — simulations, visualisations and widgets — that instructors generate with AI. Find them under Playgrounds (or Labs) and react to give the author feedback.
Not the Code Playground
The Code Playground is the code editor block inside a lesson.

title: The Library and other content areas
summary: Where reusable resources live, and how content areas are switched on per organization.
text:
Library — folders of reusable files and resources you can reference from courses.
Communities — discussion spaces.
Podcasts — audio series.
Boards — collaborative canvases.
Playgrounds — AI-generated interactive experiences.
Each area is enabled per organization in Organization settings and appears in the sidebar when on.
Reuse, don’t duplicate
Keep shared handouts and diagrams in the Library instead of uploading them to every course.

title: Signing in & accounts
summary: “You appear to be offline”, locked out after failed attempts, Google or SSO sign-in problems, unverified email.
text:
“You appear to be offline”
The app cannot reach ValidBridge. Check your connection and reload. If it keeps happening, contact support.

Locked out after several attempts
Sign-in is rate-limited after repeated failures. Wait a few minutes, or reset your password with Forgot password?.

Google sign-in or sign-in links are missing
Your organization has not enabled that method. Use email and password, or ask an admin (Users → Sign-in Methods).

SSO fails or loops
Sign in from your organization's own sign-in page and check that your email domain is allowed. Your admin manages SSO settings.

I never got the verification email
Check spam and promotions folders, then try again. See Signing in.

title: Courses, content & media
summary: A course is not visible, uploads fail, captions never finish, or an embed is blank.
text:
A course is not visible
It may be a draft, or restricted to a user group you are not in. Ask its owner to publish it or add you to the group.

An image or video will not upload
Check the format and size limits shown in the upload dialog — images are usually PNG, JPG or WebP; hosted video is MP4 or WebM.

Captions never finish
Caption generation needs AI enabled and AI credits available. Check the status in the captions panel; if it stays stuck, contact support.

A video embed is blank
The source may block embedding, or the video may be private.

Co-editing or a board is stuck on “connecting”
Live sync is temporarily unavailable. Your normal saves still work — only simultaneous editing pauses. Reload in a moment.

title: Assignments & grading
summary: Cannot submit, work not saving near a deadline, no score on a formative assignment, a grade looks wrong.
text:
I can’t submit
The deadline may have passed or you may have used all attempts. Contact your instructor.

My work stopped saving
Near the deadline you are warned before saving stops. Submit before the cut-off.

No score on my assignment
Formative assignments are ungraded by design — they unlock a model answer instead.

My grade looks wrong
Ask your instructor to review the submission.

title: AI & credits
summary: No Ask AI button, “out of credits”, or answers that seem off-topic.
text:
There is no Ask AI button
AI is switched off for your organization. An admin can turn it on under Organization → AI.

“Out of credits”
Your organization's AI credits are used up. They renew with your plan, or an admin can add more.

Answers seem off-topic
Open the Copilot from the activity you are asking about so it has the right context.

title: Contact support
summary: Who to ask, how to report a problem, and how to write a support request that gets a fast answer.
text:
Who to ask
Your organization — for access to a course, grades, roles or a payment you made — your instructor or your organization's admins can fix these directly.
ValidBridge support — for bugs, outages, account problems and anything about how the platform works. Email support@validbridge.co.ke or use Help → Report Issue or Feedback in the app.
AI Copilot — questions about course content — see Ask AI.
Write a request that gets solved quickly
What you were trying to do, and what you expected.
What happened instead — include the exact error text.
The page you were on, your role, and your organization.
A screenshot if the problem is visual.
ValidBridge is built and supported by Stratnovo Systems.
Try search first
The search box at the top of the Help Center searches every article, including these FAQs.
